committed: before js/kernels/cosmology/late/*, the validator, the oracle script and its pinned output, and before any distance, time, age, deceleration parameter, transition redshift, contour or oracle number of Prompt 255 existed. Phase 1 of the session (reading the roadmap's section 255, Operating rules 7.5, Appendix C, the register, Checkpoint V and its decisions, Carl's rulings of 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06, the existing cosmology kernel js/kernels/cosmology/flrw.js and COSMOLOGY.md, js/numeric/quadrature.js and roots.js, and the sibling gates' form for 250 and 251) preceded it and fixed nothing here from a result. The only arithmetic done before this file was input design with numpy and no Gravitas code: the scale-free ratio r(a) = F(a) / (Or + Om a + |Ok| a^2 + Ode a^(1 - 3w)) with F(a) = a^4 E(a)^2, scanned on a log grid of a, was used to pick parameter sets that bounce (r <= 0 somewhere in (0, 1]) and sets that sit close to a bounce without one; the line-of-sight integral of dz / E to z = 1e4 was evaluated to find a closed set whose light crosses the antipode. No expected value below is the output of the kernel: every one is a closed form written in the leg, the output of the oracle script (written after this file and before the kernel), a bound set by double precision or by a stated quadrature tolerance, or a count of a stated seeded ensemble.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured (a file not supplied, a tool not installed) is NOT RUN and says why, and nothing is fetched. No published distance, age, table value, cosmological parameter of a survey, licence term or citation detail is typed anywhere from memory. Every parameter set below is a round number chosen for the test and is a claim about nothing in the sky. Every authentic fact would come from a file Carl supplied under tests/fixtures/cosmology2/authentic/ with its source, its terms as read from a saved copy and its retrieval date in that directory's SOURCES.json. Failed legs are never rescued by moving a bound, re-reading a committed threshold after a result or counting a case out; the alternative is recorded as a question for Carl. Amendments are recorded in the amendments list below before any validator run that could depend on them.

(item 3), the model-page section (item 4): the consumers rule of Carl's 2026-11-05 ruling is unmet. analysisRule.R1: Units: distances in Mpc, times in Gyr, H0 in km/s/Mpc, densities as fractions of today's critical density, z dimensionless: the units of flrw.js. The speed of light is the tree's C_KMS and the Gyr per inverse Hubble time the tree's GYR_PER_INV_H0; a caller who holds metres or seconds converts.
analysisRule.R2: The Friedmann equation: E(z)^2 = Om x^3 + Or x^4 + Ok x^2 + Ode x^(3 (1 + w)), x = 1 + z, with Ok = 1 - Om - Or - Ode, so E(0) = 1 exactly in exact arithmetic. When no Ode is supplied the universe is flat (Ode = 1 - Om - Or). Radiation is one component with w = 1/3 and a density the caller supplies; no number for the CMB temperature or the neutrino count is in the kernel.
analysisRule.R3: Validated domain: H0 in (0, 1000]; Om in [0, 10]; Or in [0, 1]; Ode in [0, 10]; w in [-3, 0]; z in [0, 1e4] for distances and lookback times; every parameter finite. Outside it the kernel throws FriedmannDomainError with a code and a reason; it never returns a number for a refused set. Negative Om, Or or Ode are refused 'negative-density' (a negative dark-energy density is outside the validated domain, whatever its physical interest).
analysisRule.R4: A bounce is refused ('bounce'): with F(a) = a^4 E^2 = Or + Om a + Ok a^2 + Ode a^(1 - 3w) the set is refused when the scale-free ratio r(a) = F / (Or + Om a + |Ok| a^2 + Ode a^(1 - 3w)) is at or below zero anywhere on [1e-8, 1] (a log-spaced scan of 20000 points refined at the minimum). That covers a universe that stops contracting in the past, a closed universe dominated by Lambda with too little matter, and a set with no big bang. A recollapse in the future (a > 1) is not tested and not refused: nothing here evaluates the future.
analysisRule.R5: A closed universe's distances are D_M = (c/H0) / sqrt(|Ok|) sin(sqrt(|Ok|) D_C H0 / c), refused 'beyond-antipode' when sqrt(|Ok|) D_C H0 / c reaches pi (the light has crossed half of the closed space, D_M would be zero or negative). An open universe uses sinh, a flat one D_M = D_C. D_L = (1 + z) D_M, D_A = D_M / (1 + z), mu = 5 log10(D_L / 10 pc) with D_L in Mpc plus 25.
analysisRule.R6: The age is the integral of a da / sqrt(F(a)) from 0 to 1, the age at redshift z the same to a = 1 / (1 + z), the lookback time the integral of dz / ((1 + z) E(z)); the age by the identity lookback(z) + age(z) = age(0) is a check between two different integrals, not a definition. The age is refused 'age-unbounded' when no matter, radiation or curvature term leads at small a and the integral diverges (pure Lambda with w = -1 and Ok = 0, de Sitter).
analysisRule.R7: The deceleration parameter is q(z) = [Om x^3 + 2 Or x^4 + (1 + 3 w) Ode x^(3 (1 + w))] / (2 E^2), curvature contributing nothing. The transition redshift is the unique root of Om x^(-3 w) + 2 Or x^(1 - 3 w) + (1 + 3 w) Ode = 0 for x >= 1 (the left side increases with x for w <= 0), found by Brent's rule; it is null with the reason 'decelerating-today' when q(0) >= 0, and with 'always-accelerating' when no radiation or matter term makes the left side positive.
analysisRule.R8: The integrals are adaptive Gauss-Legendre (js/numeric/quadrature.js, 16 points per panel) in u = ln(1 + z) for distances and lookback, and in v = ln a for the age, with the tolerance and depth stated in COSMOLOGY_II.md; the age integral starts at a = 1e-10 with the leading small-a behaviour added analytically. The integrator's error estimate (the sum of its accepted panels' disagreements, which the library says is an estimate and not a bound) plus eight units of rounding on the value is returned beside every integral-based value and propagated through the geometry; an integral that does not converge is refused 'not-converged'. It is called an error estimate everywhere; B5 tests whether it covers the truth.
analysisRule.R9: The degeneracy tool: for a base cosmology, a redshift, a quantity (comoving, transverse, luminosity, angularDiameter, modulus, lookback) and two axes chosen from H0, Om, Ode, w (Ode only when the set is not flat), the contour at the base's own value of the quantity is traced by finding, for each value of the first parameter on a grid, the second parameter that reproduces the target: 64 scan points over the second parameter's range, the first sign change between two consecutive in-domain points refined by Brent's rule. A grid value with no sign change is skipped 'no-root', one whose scan points are all refused is skipped 'all-refused', and a contour never contains a point of a refused set; when the scan finds more than one sign change the first is used and the point carries multipleRoots. The local degeneracy direction at a point is the tangent (-dD/dy, dD/dx) of the contour from five-point central differences with a step of 1 percent of each parameter's scale, returned with the slope dy/dx and the gradient.
analysisRule.R10: Fixed seeded draws and fixed parameter sets are inputs. The oracle's own domain check is an independent brute-force implementation (a dense scan of 200001 points and its own rules) and its verdict on each draw is what the kernel is compared with; a draw whose scale-free ratio minimum is within 1e-4 of zero, or whose w is within 1e-9 of a bound, is flagged 'margin' by the oracle and is excluded from the agreement count (the exclusions are counted and reported).
analysisRule.R11: The consumers clause: a panel, a lesson, a viewer or the model-page section is not built while the product verdict is anything but A, and the product verdict is NOT ESTABLISHED while E1 is NOT RUN.

verdictFunction.what: the Part A kernel verdict, a function of the rows alone: A when every closed-form leg (A1 to A9), every oracle leg that was run (B1 to B5), every refusal leg (D1 to D7), the ensemble C1 and every degeneracy leg (F1 to F4) passes; B when A1 to A9, B1 to B5 and D1 to D4, D6 and D7 pass but C1, D5 or any of F1 to F4 fails: the distances, times, ages, deceleration parameter and transition redshift are claimable and the ensemble agreement or the degeneracy contours are not; C when any of A1 to A9, B1 to B5, D1 to D4, D6 or D7 fails: nothing of the kernel is claimable. The product verdict is NOT ESTABLISHED while B6 is NOT RUN. The consumers clause (a panel, a lesson, the model-page section) is unmet whatever the kernel verdict, and is met only by a product verdict of A.
